FM04.reasoning: The agent imputes missing values for spatial coordinates using the median of the combined train and test dataset, leaking test set statistics into the training data.

FM15.reasoning: The agent evaluates and optimizes the models using only RMSE, without verifying if it is robust to outliers or checking other metrics like MAE.

other_failure_modes.name: Feature Leakage Before Splitting
other_failure_modes.description: The agent performs feature engineering such as frequency encoding and group aggregations (mean/std) on the combined train and test dataset before splitting. This leaks the distribution and statistics of the test set into the training features.

other_failure_modes.name: Target Leakage via Improper Target Encoding within CV
other_failure_modes.description: The agent computes out-of-fold target encodings globally and then uses them as features in a cross-validation loop that uses the exact same folds. This causes target leakage because the training features for a given fold incorporate the targets of that fold's validation set.

summary: The agent builds a well-structured pipeline with extensive feature engineering and a proper blended ensemble of CatBoost, LightGBM, and XGBoost. However, it introduces critical data leakage by performing imputation, frequency encoding, and group aggregations on the combined train and test datasets. Furthermore, a severe target leakage occurs because the out-of-fold target encodings are computed globally and then used as features in a CV loop with identical folds, meaning the training features contain information derived from the validation targets.
